title: How can I export a child table

posts.name: Khaled Jallad
posts.cooked:
Hi,
I have added custom input fields and configuration to the Expense Claim Detail child table and need to export these customizations as part of my app so they can be installed on another site where developer mode is disabled. The parent doctype (Expense Claim) exports without issue, but the child table modifications are not being applied on the target site despite trying all the standard approaches. could you please help me

posts.name: Sudhanshu Badole
posts.cooked:
If you’ve added custom fields to a Doctype—whether a parent (like Expense Claim) or a child table (like Expense Claim Detail)—and want to move these changes to another site, here are two valid ways to do it:

Option 1: Recommended — Use Fixtures

This works reliably even in production environments (i.e. when developer_mode = 0).

Step 1: Customize Using “Customize Form”

  • Go to Customize Form
  • Select the Doctype (Expense Claim or Expense Claim Detail)
  • Add your custom fields
  • Save

These changes are stored as Custom Field and Property Setter documents.

Step 2: Add to Fixtures in hooks.py

In your app’s hooks.py:

fixtures = [
    {
        "doctype": "Custom Field",
        "filters": [
            ["dt", "in", ["Expense Claim", "Expense Claim Detail"]]
        ]
    },
    {
        "doctype": "Property Setter",
        "filters": [
            ["doc_type", "in", ["Expense Claim", "Expense Claim Detail"]]
        ]
    }
]

Step 3: Export the Fixtures

Run:

bench export-fixtures

This creates JSON files (like custom_field.json, property_setter.json) inside your app’s /fixtures folder.

Step 4: Apply on Another Site

Once you install the app or pull changes into another site, just run:

bench migrate

The fields will be applied automatically — no need for developer mode on the target site.

Option 2: Quick Dev Use — Export from Customize Form

You can also use the “Export” button at the top right of the Customize Form page.

This:

  • Exports your customizations to a JSON file
  • Lets you choose which DocTypes and fields to include
  • Useful for creating manual backups or sharing with a team

But note:

  • These JSON files won’t auto-apply on install unless you manually load them or use developer_mode = 1
  • Not ideal for deployment to staging/production

Understanding the Confusion: Parent vs Child Doctype

  • Expense Claim is a parent Doctype
  • Expense Claim Detail is a child table, but it’s still a separate Doctype
  • You must include both in your fixtures or Export if you customize both

Child tables aren’t magically included — if you forget to list the child Doctype, its custom fields won’t move.
